description: The same application, the same documents, a different clerk, a different result. Everyone who deals with these systems knows this and none of them can prove it in their own case.
energy_note: Refused by a person who was having a bad morning.

aspect: Discretion is unappealable precisely because it is discretion
description: Where the decision-maker is entitled to weigh factors, there is no error of law to appeal. Being wrongly assessed is not a ground; being unlawfully assessed is, and the two are hard to distinguish from outside.
energy_note: Not wrong enough to appeal, wrong enough to ruin it.

aspect: SCENARIO - the eligible woman with no insurance
description: She is entitled to the coverage. The clerk enters her status incorrectly, the system generates a refusal, and the refusal becomes the record. Eleven months later an ombudsman agrees she was always eligible. The surgery happened in month four, uninsured.
energy_note: Correct all along, and bankrupt anyway.

aspect: The apology, where it comes, restores nothing
description: Systems that correct errors rarely compensate for the interval. The finding that you were right is issued after the consequences have completed.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the ban that evaporated twice
description: A Gaza physician was refused a permit to reach Palestinian Medical Council exams in Ramallah in 2018 on unspecified security grounds. Gisha petitioned the High Court; the ban was retracted before the hearing and 3,000 ILS costs were awarded against the state. In February 2019 she was refused again, on unspecified security grounds, and the state withdrew immediately after the second petition.
energy_note: A security threat twice, and never once in front of a judge.
